Hi Lydia — thanks for the details and the attachments. Quick read-through: traffic profile looks spiky (short bursts) and your memory trace confirms large KV footprint at 64k. A few clarifying items before a precise estimate:

1) Expected average prompt length (tokens) vs max context used for retrievals.
2) Generation distribution (how often do users generate 2k vs 10k tokens).
3) SLOs: p50/p95 latency targets for the generation portion.

Ballpark based on our initial read and typical Lumen-70B characteristics:
- Unquantized weights (FP16) ~140GB ephemeral in-memory weights (per replica)
- KV cache at 64k in FP16 range: ~110-140GB depending on head count
- If we use 4-bit weight quantization plus KV offload to NVMe, per-replica GPU memory need can be reduced into the ~60-90GB range, which maps to A100-80GB (1–2 GPUs per replica depending on design)

Rough fleet recommendation for your stated QPS and concurrency (initial): 6–8 replicas sized for 50 qps aggregate with headroom, using a mixture of 80GB GPUs and NVMe-backed KV offload. If you want to avoid NVMe for compliance, we should plan for 12–16 x A100-80GB equivalents (higher cost).

Marissa (SE) and Karthik (infra) — can you validate the KV numbers and give a short pod layout?

I can jump on a 30m call tomorrow to walk through assumptions.

Best,
Rishi

Folks — dug into the attachments and ran a quick emulation with our allocator. Highlights and concrete numbers (estimates, conservative):

Assumptions: Lumen-70B: 70B params, transformer, 64k KV tokens max, 32 attention heads, hidden dim 12,288 (approx). Generation average 2k tokens, peak path up to 10k occasionally.

Raw estimates (per active replica):
- Weights (FP16): ~140GB
- Weights (4-bit qint4 w/ 8-bit group scaling): ~38–45GB (includes dequant buffers)
- KV cache size @64k, FP16: ~120GB
- KV cache @8-bit: ~60GB; @4-bit: ~30–35GB (we've measured ~2.9x reduction vs FP16 with our kernel+compaction)
- Runtime overhead (optimizer buffers, activation buffers for generation, temp): ~10–15GB depending on batching

Two common deployment patterns we recommend: 
A) NVMe-backed KV offload + quantized weights (q4) on single 80GB GPU per replica:
   - GPU resident: quant weights 40GB + activations ~10GB + working set ~5–10GB = ~60GB used
   - KV persisted/compressed on fast NVMe and streamed: effective GPU RAM <80GB
   - Pod: 1 x A100-80GB GPU + 2 x NVMe (high throughput)
   - Notes: lowest cost, meets latency if NVMe is fast and network hop low

B) In-memory KV, no NVMe (compliance-sensitive):
   - Plan for weights (q4) + full KV in GPU RAM -> ~40GB + 35GB = ~75–80GB per replica minimum (tight), realistic safer choice: 2 x 80GB GPUs per replica to split KV and activations
   - Pod: 2 x A100-80GB GPUs with NCCL/pinned memory layout

Fleet sizing for your profile (50 qps peak, 100 concurrent users, p95 gen latency target sub-800ms):
- Mode A (NVMe offload): 8 replicas x 1 GPU = handles steady-state with autoscale to 12 replicas for bursts
- Mode B (no NVMe): 6 replicas x 2 GPUs = capacity equivalent, higher cost but simpler data path

Cost/Quality tradeoff: q4 (4-bit) is very attractive for memory reduction — in our internal evals quality delta vs bf16 is small for Lumen on retrieval-heavy prompts, but you should run a short eval with your prompt set. If hallucination tolerance is low, we recommend q8 for production until we complete joint evals.

I attached a small per-replica calculation sheet in the Drive link. If Nicola from procurement wants numbers for the SOW I can produce a scoped price with both modes.

- Marissa

Quick infra note on autoscaling and pooling:

- Suggest autoscale policy: baseline 6 replicas (warm), scale up by 1 replica per additional 4 qps sustained beyond baseline for 10 minutes, burst buffer of 4 replicas for short spikes.
- Use mixed-instance pool: prefer A100-80GB instances with NVMe for Mode A. We'll reserve NVMe IOPS and local networking (placement groups) to keep NVMe streaming latency predictable.
- Fallback policy: route non-critical or exploratory queries to Lumen-7B-32k (model variant) if the pool is saturated. This saves ~3–4x cost while keeping UX acceptable.

Operational checklist:
1) Run short joint evals (Marissa) comparing q4/q8/bf16 on your prompt set (3-day job)
2) Confirm compliance constraints (Lydia) re: NVMe persistence and encryption at rest
3) Procurement: sign temporary reserved capacity for 3 months to lock price during POC

I'll prepare a pod template (k8s + NCCL hints + NVMe topology) and drop in Drive by EOD.

- Karthik
